title: Quantum burst realignment and rolling-reset hedge for reserved capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Reserved capacity customers are experiencing transient billing and throttling anomalies when tenant usage crosses midnight or monthly boundaries in presence of rolling/overlapping quota windows (timezones, DST, and staggered tenant epoch anchors). These anomalies manifest as short-lived over-throttles or unbilled bursts when the quota reset logic and the reserved-pool allocation scheduler race.

Goal: Implement a conservative, backwards-compatible "rolling-reset hedge" that realigns tenant burst allocations (quantum bursts) across epoch boundaries without causing negative balances or double-charging. The feature must be opt-in via feature flag, safe for canarying, and provide deterministic, idempotent recovery if a controller-level reconciliation fails.

Scope: Engineering work to add a soft-anchoring layer to the quota ledger, a slipstream recovery runner to repair interleaved epoch drift, and a hedging policy in the quota allocator that reserves a small safety buffer during known boundary windows. This ticket covers design, core implementation, migration/backfill for ledger rows, operational metrics, and canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: No customer sees an unexpected negative quota balance after a rolling reset across any timezone boundary in canary customers (verified by smoke test).
Allocator never double-allocates reserved tokens during epoch boundary windows under synthetic load (load-test pass).
Backfill/migration can convert existing per-tenant ledger rows to include soft_anchor metadata with < 1 minute downtime for the reconciliation job controller.
Reconciliation runner is idempotent and safe to run concurrently; unit and integration tests cover duplicate execution and partial failure scenarios.
Dashboards expose per-tenant hedge usage, recovered slipstream events, and a new 'reset-variance' metric; alert thresholds configured for >0.1% of tenants affected in a day.
implementation_notes: Introduce `soft_anchor_epoch` and `anchor_version` columns into quota_ledger (nullable string/int). Use migration job that writes new rows instead of in-place updates for easier rollback.

Allocator change: when `now` within configured boundary window (tenant timezone midnight +/- configured jitter) use hedging policy that keeps a safety buffer of 0.5% of tenant reserved capacity or min(10 tokens). This buffer is released after the slipstream recovery completes.

Slipstream recovery runner: periodic controller that scans tenants with overlapping/nearby epochs, computes deterministic realignment plan, writes an idempotent checkpoint entry, and emits events to reconcile live allocators. The runner must be throttled and leader-elected for HA clusters.

Idempotency: recovery writes a reconciliation token with a monotonic sequence (reconciliation_id) to ledger checkpoint table; subsequent runs detect completed IDs and skip reapplication. Ensure reconciliation operations are transactional with the ledger write path.
Telemetry: emit events `quota.hedge.start`, `quota.hedge.release`, `quota.slipstream.recover`, `quota.reset.variance` with tenant_id, reconciliation_id, pre/post balances, and reason code.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gate in config: `quota.rolling_reset_hedge_v1` default OFF.
Step 1: Merge core changes behind flag and run DB migration in read-only mode to verify schema (canary cluster).
Step 2: Enable hedging policy for 5 low-risk reserved tenants for 24h. Monitor `reset-variance` and hedge metrics.
Step 3: Expand to 100 reserved tenants across regions and timezones over 48h; keep rollback playbook ready.
Step 4: If stable, enable for all reserved tenants with gradual ramp and coordinated migration job to backfill `soft_anchor_epoch` values.
Rollback: disable flag and run compensating reconciliation that clears safety buffers and replays any pending allocations into the standard path.
tests: Unit tests for ledger migration and anchor_version semantics (edge cases: DST, leap second).
Integration test simulating two allocators racing over epoch boundary; assert single allocation and no negative balance.
Load test with 10k tenants where 1% have staggered midnight anchors; measure throttle errors and billing deltas.
Chaos test: kill recovery runner mid-reconciliation and ensure idempotent retry repairs state.

2026-03-06 Lina Morales (SRE): Leader election for slipstream runner needs to use cluster lease TTL=60s to avoid double recovery; SRE will provide helper library.
2026-03-10 Marcus Chen: Implemented telemetry events and unit tests for idempotent checkpointing. Running canary on 3 tenants now. Initial metrics look good; no double-charges observed.
